# Green Alert
Green Alert requires the following steps to be taken in order to make an arrest or search unless security has probable cause.
## 1) Obtain a search warrant or arrest warrant.
### a) Contraband found Contraband found after a search warrant is served constitutes probable cause for an immediate arrest.
### b) Must Be Signed The search warrant or arrest warrant must be signed by the Prosecutor, Clerk, or Chief Justice; in their absence (or under extenuating circumstances where they are not available in a timely manner), the Warden or Head of Security may sign the warrant instead.
- The Captain can always issue arrest warrants, regardless of circumstances; officers should not seek them out to sign warrants unless the Justice Department, Warden, and Head of Security are unavailable.
-If there is no Prosecutor, Clerk, or Chief Justice on station, the Warden or Head of Security must sign the warrant.
### c) Make a duplicate of the warrant Make a duplicate of the warrant to leave in security, in case the original warrant gets destroyed, stolen, or lost.
### d) Mandatory Information The search warrant or arrest warrant does not need to be detailed, but the following information is mandatory: - 1) The name of the suspect being searched or arrested. - 2) The name of the person highest in the Security Chain of Command when the warrant was issued. - 3) The time during the shift that the warrant was issued. - 4) The reason the warrant is being made. - 5) The evidence supporting the warrant.
## 2) Find the suspect and serve them the arrest or search warrant.
### a) Follow the Method of Escalation (Ordinary Arrests).
### b) For search warrants For search warrants, serve them the search warrant and tell them that this is a mandated search, and that failure to comply with the warrant will be treated as obstruction of justice.
- If no contraband is found, the suspect is free to go, regardless of any rudeness or (non obstructive) reluctance to the search.
- It is at the Officer’s discretion what is considered “obstructive”.
- If contraband is found, this constitutes probable cause for an arrest.
On green alert, all searches that do not have a warrant and do not have probable cause must be voluntary. - Security members can ask any crew member to search them. - Crew has the right to decline these searches for any reason (including not giving a reason). - Security can obtain search warrants for crew that have declined to be voluntarily searched; in this case, the suspect must submit to the search. - Denial of search is not probable cause nor cause for suspicion.
Departmental Searches always require a warrant on Green Alert and Blue Alert. - This warrant must be signed by the Chief Justice; in their absence, or under circumstances where they are not available in a timely manner, their Clerk may sign instead. - The Captain can always issue departmental search warrants, regardless of circumstances; officers should not seek them out to sign this warrant unless the Justice Department is unavailable. - If the Chief Justice, Clerk, and Captain are all unavailable, the Head of Security may issue a departmental search warrant. - When possible, inform the command member in charge of the department to be searched before the search takes place. - Officers must have an already signed departmental search warrant before searching a department. - It is advisable to duplicate this warrant and leave one copy in security before conducting the search. - Destruction of the warrant after it has been presented to a relevant departmental member does not void the warrant nor the search.
# Blue Alert
Blue alert requires the same arrest protocol as Green Alert, but does *not* require the same search procedure. Blue alert should not be called to search a specific individual or otherwise bypass creating a warrant.
Instead, on Blue Alert, security may stop and search any crew member, regardless of suspicion or probable cause. All individual searches are non-voluntary; departmental searches and Implant Searches still require a warrant.
Security should attempt to be courteous when conducting these searches; the Method of Escalation (Ordinary Arrests) should be followed. - Inform the crew member that this is a mandated search, and that failure to comply will be treated as obstruction of justice. - If no contraband is found, the suspect is free to go, regardless of any rudeness or (non obstructive) reluctance to the search. - It is at the Officer’s discretion what is considered “obstructive”. If contraband is found, this constitutes probable cause for an arrest.
# Red Alert
All arrests and searches, except for Implant Searches, can be made as if there is probable cause during Red Alert; no warrants are required. The Method of Escalation (Ordinary Arrests) must still be followed for ordinary arrests and searches that are not deemed to fall under the Method of Escalation (Station Threats).
While no warrants are required for any searches (other than implant searches) including departmental searches on Red Alert, security must prioritize dealing with the active threat(s) over searching crew or departments. Red alert should not be called to bypass creating a warrant.
# Other Alerts
On Yellow, White, and Violet alerts, search, arrest, and gear/armor procedures should assume Blue Alert. The Captain or Head of Security must inform the crew through an Announcement another alert level is to be assumed. On Orange, Delta, and Gamma alerts, search, arrest, and gear/armor procedures should assume Red alert.
# Implant Search Procedure
In order to conduct an implant search, officers must have reasonable suspicion of a contraband implant. In order to have reasonable suspicion, an implanter with their DNA must have been found or they must have been witnessed performing an action that is not possible without an implant.
The HOS, Captain, and Chief Justice can all issue implant search warrants.
An implant search warrant must be signed off by the Chief Medical Officer and the Head of Security. If the HOS is unavailable the Warden may sign off in their place. If the CMO is unavailable the Captain may sign off in their place. If the CMO and Captain are unavailable, another member of medical staff may sign off in their place.
Implant search warrants always require two approvals. If the Captain issues the warrant they can not also sign off in place of the CMO.
The implant search must be conducted by either a member of medical or the corpsman. Only in the absence of all medical professionals and the corpsman should security carry it out themselves. The implant search should be conducted in private, and with only the individual conducting the search and one additional officer for safety.
Any contraband or restricted items found should be handled in the usual method. Any psionic crystals found should be turned over to the mantis or the Epistemics department. Any legal implants found should be returned to the individual upon completion of the search.
